title: Fourier coefficient bound for random tuples
statement: Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube whose nonzero Fourier coefficients are indexed only by subsets of size $k$. Choose a tuple $a$ uniformly from all maps from a $k$-element set to an $n$-element set, allowing repeated values, and let $A$ be its image. Then the expected squared Fourier coefficient indexed by $A$ is at most $k!/n^k$ times the total Fourier weight of $f$ at level $k$.
hypotheses_covered: A real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
Every nonzero Fourier coefficient is indexed by a subset of size $k$
